title: Introduce responsive row-tiling and column-priority overlays for large datasets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our current virtualized table handles uniform row heights and single-column focus patterns well, but real customer datasets often include heterogeneous rows (multi-line cells, badges, nested metadata) and dense result sets where users need to scan priorities quickly. This ticket proposes a design pattern that combines responsive row-tiling (variable-height virtualization-friendly layout) with a visual column-priority overlay that surfaces the most relevant columns at different density modes and breakpoints. Goals: 1) maintain 99th-percentile scroll latency targets under realistic workloads, 2) improve user scan efficiency for wide tables without forcing permanent column-pinning, 3) keep keyboard and screen-reader accessibility intact across density modes.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec and component tokens for row-tiling that support variable heights and graceful virtualization fallbacks (single-line fallback for extremely constrained devices)
Prototype in Figma demonstrating three density modes: relaxed, compact, micro — with overlay behavior for column-priority on hover/keyboard-focus
Interaction spec for keyboard-first column-priority activation (e.g., Alt+P opens overlay) and ARIA roles for overlay content
Engineering checklist that maps to performance budgets (initial render <120ms, sustained scroll 99th <40ms on tested dataset)
Usability test results from at least 6 participants showing reduced time-to-find primary column data by >=15% vs baseline
decisions: Use progressive enhancement: default virtualization assumes fixed-height rows, row-tiling enabled via data attribute when variable content is detected
Column-priority overlay will be transient (overlay layer) rather than collapsing columns by default to avoid layout shift
Density modes remain explicit user settings (Relaxed / Compact / Micro) and will persist to workspace preferences
We will implement accessibility affordances first (keyboard trigger, focus trapping, descriptive ARIA labels) before visual polish
engineering_notes: ENG owners: evaluate existing virtualization lib for support of variable heights; recommend adding incremental height cache and 'in-view' estimation layer
Suggested implementation: introduce 'row-tiling-mode' opt-in prop on Table component; when enabled, render a lightweight measurement layer during idle frames to populate height cache
Benchmark plan: synthetic dataset with 50k rows (mix single-line, 3-line, 8-line rows) to measure memory and GC behavior; target memory delta <20% vs fixed-row baseline
Fallback strategy: on low-memory devices or when measurement budget exceeded, collapse to single-line rendering with tooltip expansion for overflow content
qa_notes: Create automated visual regression tests for three density modes across viewport sizes
End-to-end tests for keyboard activation of column-priority overlay and ARIA announcements
Performance smoke tests using the provided 50k synthetic dataset; capture frame rate and 99th percentile scroll latency
Cross-browser checks: Chrome (latest), Safari (latest), Firefox (latest) and Electron builds
review_comments: PM feedback (Jordan Lee): prefer overlay to be dismissible via Esc and click-away — align with global modal patterns
Eng feedback (Rina Morales): measurement layer needs to be cancellable and throttle-friendly; add an opt-out flag for Dedicated deployments with strict memory budgets
Accessibility review (Samir Kapoor): ensure column-priority overlay is reachable via Landmark/Region roles and provides a concise summary string for screen readers
Design critique (Leah Ortiz): micro-density may become too cramped for touch; propose increased touch target on mobile and use compact mode there
